questions.q: What makes PostgreSQL's ARRAY column type distinctive compared to SQL Server, Oracle, and MySQL?
options: It's a genuine native column type for holding a list of values; none of the other three platforms have this as a first-class type
It's identical to a comma-separated VARCHAR column
It only works for numeric values, never text
SQL Server has the exact same ARRAY type under a different name
questions.explain: A single PostgreSQL column can genuinely BE an array, something T-SQL/Oracle/MySQL have no first-class equivalent for.

questions.q: What does unnest() do to an array column?
options: Expands the array into one row per element
Deletes the array column from the table
Converts the array into a JSONB value
Sorts the array's elements alphabetically
questions.explain: unnest() is the bridge from one row with an array column to one row per array element, useful for querying or joining.

questions.q: What's the key difference between PostgreSQL's JSON and JSONB types?
options: JSON stores an exact text copy; JSONB stores a parsed binary representation that's faster to query and indexable
JSON and JSONB are exactly identical, just different names for the same storage
JSONB is deprecated in favor of JSON
JSON can only store arrays, JSONB can only store objects
questions.explain: JSONB's binary, parsed storage is what makes it indexable and generally the right choice for real application use.

questions.q: What's the difference between the -> and ->> JSONB access operators?
options: -> returns JSON (keeps quotes/nesting); ->> returns TEXT (unwraps to a plain string)
-> and ->> are interchangeable with no difference
-> only works on arrays, ->> only works on objects
-> deletes a key, ->> reads a key
questions.explain: -> preserves the JSON type of the result, while ->> unwraps the result to plain text.

questions.q: What does the @> JSONB operator test, and what index type commonly accelerates it?
options: Whether the left JSONB value contains the right one, accelerated by a GIN index
Whether two JSONB values are exactly equal, accelerated by a B-tree index
Whether a JSONB value is valid JSON, accelerated by a hash index
Whether a JSONB column is NULL, requiring no index at all
questions.explain: @> is the containment operator, and GIN indexes are specifically built to make containment queries on JSONB genuinely fast.
